chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Hasan ibn Nu'aym, from Mis'mam al-Kirdi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

Whoever relieves a believer of a hardship, Allah will relieve him of the hardships of the Hereafter, and he will emerge from his grave with a cool heart. And whoever feeds a hungry person, Allah will feed him the fruits of Paradise. And whoever gives him a drink of water, Allah will give him a drink from the sealed wine (Rahiq al-Makhtum).
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for relieving a believer's hardship according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-A'mal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight the reciprocal nature of divine mercy, where alleviating a believer's worldly distress secures relief from the anxieties of the grave and the Hereafter. The narration specifically links physical sustenance—feeding and watering—to spiritual rewards, citing 'Rahiq al-Makhtum' (the sealed wine of Paradise) as a metaphor for pure, eternal bliss, thereby elevating simple acts of charity to profound acts of worship.
